sections.overview: Triops cancriformis is a branchiopod crustacean of the order Notostraca, commonly called a tadpole shrimp.
sections.identification: Like other tadpole shrimps, it has a distinctive shielded body and a long, forked tail.
sections.habitat: It lives in temporary freshwater pools that periodically dry out.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet information is sparse; field literature reports feeding on organic detritus.
sections.behavior: Its active aquatic phase follows refilling, and surveys commonly find adults a few weeks after a pool fills.
sections.reproduction: Populations use different reproductive modes, and each mode can produce dormant cysts that survive drought in pond sediment.
sections.ecology: It belongs to a mainly Palearctic Triops lineage, whereas the closely related T. longicaudatus–newberryi lineage is largely American.
sections.conservation: In Britain it is treated as a rare, survey-priority species; this regional concern should not be mistaken for a global assessment.
